lines: Good morning. I’m Hannah Thibedeau, and this is your Palindrome News brief.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said that Canada could turn to Chinese automakers if trade negotiations with U.S, The Associated Press reports.
IIHF confirms Russia will not compete at world juniors in Canada, The Canadian Press reports.

An aviation management expert says Canada is less likely than the United States to ground flights nationwide as that country did on Friday afternoon, calling the Canadian system a model its southern neighbours should look to, The Canadian Press reports.

There were no frigid temperatures or even any snow on the ground, but the spirit of Christmas was still in the air for the annual Santa Claus Parade down the northern portion of Albert Street on Sunday, The Canadian Press reports.
Officials say a tanker’s steering failed before it crashed into a cruise ship in New Orleans, The Associated Press reports.
Asian shares mostly declined Monday as investors’ worries over the future of the artificial intelligence trade extended into another week following Nvidia’s fallout, The Canadian Press reports.
That’s your brief. We’ll keep watching, so you don’t have to.
